points: This carryover audit supplements only G2 and G3; G0/G4/G5/G1 are inherited from the captured record.

A real Chrome session read the complete first two US-English pages without CAPTCHA. The natural exact query is dominated by generic secure-MCP tutorials, Workspace/database/SecOps servers, Secure Source Manager instance pages and Cloud Run builds; page two continues with governance, gateways and unrelated products.

G2=pass: the original two-page SERP has an extreme Secure-Source-Manager exactness quality cliff and no task-completing media or homepage takeover. A quoted source/product query reveals the release-note signal and official guide through the product overview, confirming the gap is indexing/discovery rather than task absence.

Google's exact official guide, updated 2026-08-18 UTC, completes setup: instance/repository prerequisites, MCP Tool User and repository roles, OAuth, regional endpoint, HTTP transport, toolset endpoints, tools, prompts, Model Armor and IAM policies.

G3=pass: only that official guide completes the exact product workflow. Generic secure-MCP and custom Cloud Run tutorials solve different tasks, and the original two pages contain no independent Secure Source Manager implementation.
This is not veto_window_bet because only one exact implementation exists; no second already-built page is merely awaiting indexing.

Window estimate is weeks, expiring 2026-09-20. The guide is two days old and not yet surfaced for the natural query, creating a narrow discovery window while the wider managed-MCP ecosystem grows quickly.

Invalidation conditions: two free end-to-end Secure Source Manager MCP guides enter the natural SERP; Google publishes a dedicated codelab; regional endpoint, toolset paths, OAuth scope, MCP Tool User/repository roles, or tool inventory changes.
